clue.text: Window that is blue and white perhaps

parts.note: the sky is blue, so blue can stand for the sky
white is an example of a light colour, as opposed to a dark one

explanation.surface: A description of a window that shows a blue and white view, presumably of sky and cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof window set into a ceiling to admit daylight is this kind of window.

clue.text: Katharine embraced artilleryman in combative sport

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one name wraps around the other piece

parts.note: Kate is the usual short form of Katharine
RA stands for Royal Artillery, so a gunner in it

explanation.surface: A woman named Katharine hugged a gunner during a martial contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery is the British army's gunnery regiment, so any artilleryman is a crossword gunner.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese martial art of unarmed fighting with strikes and kicks is a combative sport.

clue.text: Replacing early bird

indicators.note: replacing the letters means putting them back in a different order, a rearrangement of the word next to it

explanation.surface: Someone swapping out the proverbial early bird that catches the worm.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen kept for egg production is called by this name, since she lays.

clue.text: Four brave and noble outside go in search of adventure

indicators.note: outside says the longer word sits around the shorter one

parts.note: gallant describes a knightly person who is brave and noble
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A knight, brave and noble, steps out to seek adventure, four of them perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four' at the start looks like a count of knights, but it only supplies the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam about pleasure-seeking is to wander in search of fun and excitement, close to seeking adventure.

clue.text: Three times wash new vehicle

parts.note: tri- is the prefix meaning three or threefold

indicators.note: new says the letters of wash are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to wash a new car three times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three times' looks like a repeat instruction for the washing, but it is just the numeric prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal-powered three-wheeled rickshaw is a form of passenger vehicle.

clue.text: Frenchman upset saint, one appearing to be praying

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a French gentleman

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of saint are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A Frenchman upsets a saint, and someone looks to be at prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one appearing to be praying' is the whole definition: the insect is named for its prayer-like pose.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying insect holds its forelegs folded as if in prayer while waiting for prey.

clue.text: Symbol of decreasing significance

parts.note: read as a sign meaning something matters less; really the arithmetic sign signifying subtraction, a decrease

explanation.definitionFit: The subtraction sign is the symbol that signifies taking away, so decreasing a number.

clue.text: Dotcom company's gain?

parts.note: a dotcom firm trades on the internet, so its earnings after costs are jokingly earnings from the web

explanation.definitionFit: Earnings left after all expenses are deducted, with the first word punning on the internet.

clue.text: One with Ronald has task to be undertaken on ornamental gates

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Ron is the short form of the name Ronald
work means a task or job

explanation.surface: Someone working with a man called Ronald has a job to do on some decorative gates.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative gates are typically made of wrought metal, the kind of craft described by this term.

clue.text: Team from Plymouth, we hear, or lochgilphead area

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: Plymouth Argyle is the football club of the English city of Plymouth

explanation.surface: A choice between a Plymouth football team and a Scottish district.
explanation.walkthrough: Plymouth Argyle is an English football club; the name sounds like the Scottish county, whose administrative centre is Lochgilphead.
explanation.definitionFit: Lochgilphead is the administrative town of this west Highland Scottish county and council region.

clue.text: Key to fire-lighting

parts.note: reads like the essential secret of making a fire; also the car key that starts the engine firing

explanation.definitionFit: This is both the starting of combustion and the switch, turned by a key, that fires an engine.

clue.text: Pisces?

parts.note: Pisces is the zodiac constellation of the fishes, so a fish made of stars

explanation.definitionFit: Pisces is a group of stars pictured as fish, which the sea creature's name literally describes.

clue.text: Bad characters joined up perhaps

parts.note: suggests villains enlisting together; really poorly formed letters written in a joined, cursive hand

explanation.definitionFit: Messy handwriting is badly formed letters, often run together in a hurried cursive.

clue.text: Striking way to live dangerously

parts.note: striking matches recklessly is a literal case of the idiom for taking foolish risks

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to court danger or take reckless risks, literally seen in striking matches.

clue.text: Left former PM in the capital

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
Tony Blair was a British prime minister from 1997 to 2007

explanation.surface: A former prime minister has left and is now living in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT BLAIR is the capital of India's Andaman and Nicobar Islands; the clue hides that it is a capital elsewhere than London.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the administrative seat of the Indian Andaman and Nicobar Islands territory.

clue.text: One who is turning the screw?

definitions.text: One who is turning the screw?

parts.words: One who is turning the screw?
parts.note: turning the screw means increasing pressure on someone; literally it is fastening something more firmly

explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something that makes a fitting more secure, or squeezes harder, is this.

clue.text: Concerned with open country

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in a letter heading
public means open to all

explanation.surface: Someone involved with the open countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A state with an elected head rather than a monarch is a kind of nation.

clue.text: Concentrated on going after funny bone

indicators.note: going after says the first-named piece follows the second in the answer

parts.note: merry means jolly or funny
thought on means concentrated on

explanation.surface: Someone focused on chasing after a funny bone, the elbow nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: The funny bone is the elbow, a decoy; the bone meant is the wishbone of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for the forked wishbone of a fowl, pulled apart for luck.

clue.text: Way a heavenly body moved?

parts.note: a heavenly body may sound like an attractive person, but a planet travelled round its sun along a path

explanation.definitionFit: A planet or moon circled another body, travelling in a curved path around it.

clue.text: Get at one in brown cover

indicators.note: in says the single letter goes inside the word for the skin colour

parts.note: a tan is the brown colour covering sunbathed skin
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone getting at a person wrapped in a brown jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get at' reads as a phrase meaning nag, but 'at' is taken as written and 'Get' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach or achieve a goal is to gain it, a synonym.

clue.text: Restrained scoundrel alongside border

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel
a flower bed or border is a strip of planted ground

explanation.surface: A rogue was held back beside a garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: A border in British gardening is a long flower bed along a path or wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Held in check or kept under control, as a horse by its bit.

clue.text: Dated record

parts.note: sounds like an old-fashioned vinyl disc; really a log of entries each marked with its date

explanation.definitionFit: A daily journal is an account of events with each entry headed by its day.

clue.text: City entrance west of livingston

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A city gateway situated to the west of a place called Livingston.
explanation.walkthrough: Bathgate is a town in West Lothian, Scotland, just west of the new town of Livingston.
explanation.definitionFit: This West Lothian town lies a few miles westward of Livingston, so the location identifies it.

clue.text: Involved in delivering our daily fruit

indicators.note: involved in says the letters lie wrapped up within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Delivering our daily supply of fruit and produce.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-skinned fruit of the squash family, often dried and hollowed for use.

clue.text: Excuses worker, that's nice!

parts.note: pleas are excuses offered in defence
a worker ant is the commonest crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone pleased that an employee has made excuses: how nice!
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable and enjoyable, a close synonym for a nice thing or person.

clue.text: Sticky sweet made aunt go mad

indicators.note: mad means crazed, so the letters of the two words beside it go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A chewy confection that drove an aunt crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts is a toothsome treat.

clue.text: Disease of the most contemptible kind

definitions.meaning: an illness caused by lack of vitamin C
an old word for mean, worthless or despicable

explanation.definitionFit: It names the sailors' vitamin-deficiency illness, and as an adjective means base or despicable.

clue.text: Laughing at Edward back on a horse

indicators.note: back says the short name is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: Ed is the short form of the name Edward
riding means mounted on a horse

explanation.surface: Edward is back in the saddle on a horse while people laugh at him.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking or ridiculing someone is jeering at them, scornful amusement.
